name: error-reporting
body: A validation error states file, line when known, full path, what is wrong and how to fix it, and every error carries this same shape whether one is reported or every one is. By default the first error found in the fixed deterministic validation order is reported — `kalide start`, and `kalide check` without `--all` — while `kalide check --all` reports every error found, in that order. The file part of the location follows native-display-paths: it is the file's path spelled as the user's own OS spells paths — the OS separator only, never mixed, and each directory's long name — and for a slide it is the slide's deck-relative path (e.g. `slides/3-team.md`), never an absolute path. On macOS and Linux the example error reads `slides/3-team.md:12 › column[1] › people[0] › name: required — add a name: value`; the same error on Windows reads `slides\3-team.md:12 › column[1] › people[0] › name: required — add a name: value`. Same text in terminal and browser error page, and the `kalide check --json` report carries each error's file, line, path, message and suggestion. The same path form extends to nested section instances (e.g. `columns[2] › blocks[1]`, nested-section-validation), so the notation is uniform at any containment depth.
